# JAMA IM: Extended hospital stays in MA vs traditional Medicare

- Citation: McGarry BE, Wilcock AD, Gandhi AD, Grabowski DC, Barnett ML. "Extended Hospital Stays in Medicare Advantage and Traditional Medicare." JAMA Internal Medicine 185(11), published online 2025-09-08. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2025.4411
- Year: 2025
- Tier: 1 (peer-reviewed)
- Sample / method: retrospective cohort, difference-in-differences; MedPAR plus enrollment data, Jan 2017 to Sep 2023; 89.3M admissions (20% sample for adjusted models).
- Key findings:
  - Mean length of stay: MA rose from 6.0 to 7.1 days; traditional Medicare from 5.8 to 6.3 days.
  - In Q3 2023, MA admissions discharged to a SNF were 3.1 percentage points (95% CI 2.6-3.6) more likely to last 14+ days than traditional Medicare admissions.
  - The authors name prior authorization and narrow post-acute networks as "plausible explanations".
- Limits: observational, so no causal claim; the period spans COVID. The cost figure in trade press ($5.5B) isn't verified here, so don't use it.
